questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: Why a query with no time limit can hold a lock longer than any timeout elsewhere
questions.learningObjective: Explain why an untimed query can outlast every other session's timeout
questions.stem: Explain why a query with no time limit can keep a lock held longer than any timeout configured elsewhere in the system.

answer.exemplar: A statement timeout is set per session and applies only to statements issued by that session. A reporting query that sets no timeout therefore runs until it finishes, and for that whole time it holds the row locks it touched. Other services may enforce short timeouts of their own, but their timeouts govern how long they will wait, not how long the reporter will hold the lock. Every one of them can give up while the lock is still held, so the effective hold is bounded by the query rather than by any timeout in the system.

questions.explanation: Timeouts limit how long a session waits, not how long another session holds a lock. A query with no timeout can therefore keep the lock past every other session's deadline.
questions.hint: Consider whose timeout governs whose statement.
